activities.name: Long-drive Delhi → Manali – scenic Himalayan ascent (self‑drive or hired car)
Evening stroll on Mall Road – short walk, local shops, sunset view

meals.breakfast: Packed breakfast on the road – sandwiches, boiled eggs, fruit

lunch.description: Thali at a dhaba near Kullu – dal, rice, chapati, pickle
lunch.location_note: near Kullu, approx 130 km from Delhi stop

dinner.description: Hearty Himachali madra (lentil‑yogurt curry) with plain rice
Chicken tikka masala with butter naan – crowd‑friendly sit‑down
Mountain‑view rooftop restaurant – butter lobster with garlic butter rice

days.notes: First day is travel‑heavy; keep hydration levels high, rest early to recover from the 13‑15 h drive.

activities.name: Visit Hadimba Devi Temple – quiet cedar forest, short ascent (≈15 min walk)
Vashisht Hot Springs – dip in mineral‑rich baths, optional foot‑massages

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel – poha, curd, fresh fruit

lunch.description: Paneer butter masala with steamed rice near Hadimba Temple
lunch.location_note: ≈1 km from the temple, in the Old Manali market area

dinner.description: Local trout fry with mustard greens (locally sourced) – Himachali style
Veg thali with dal, rice, chapati, and sweet curd – family‑friendly
Upscale dining at a riverside lounge – lamb rogan josh with saffron rice

days.notes: Gentle cultural day; temple steps are modest, hot springs provide a relaxing soak after travel.

activities.name: Solang Ropeway & Paragliding – 30 min ropeway ascent, optional tandem paragliding (bookable)
Zorbing or Snow‑play (seasonal) – short 20‑minute session on the snow‑covered slope

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – aloo paratha with curd and chai

lunch.description: Dhabba‑style aloo paratha with pickles, served near the ropeway base
lunch.location_note: ≈5 km from Manali centre, on the Solang road

dinner.description: Kashmiri chai with baked momos (vegetable) – local snack
Chicken curry with basmati rice – safe for group dining
Premium mountain‑lodge dinner – grilled salmon with herb butter and roasted potatoes

days.notes: Adventure‑focused day; keep warm layers handy for high‑altitude chill. Ropeway tickets can be booked via local operators.

activities.name: Rohtang Pass Day‑tour – early departure, permit arranged through official portal, scenic drive, short photo stops

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast – boiled eggs, toast, tea

lunch.description: Packed picnic – sandwich, boiled potatoes, fruit, and bottled water (enjoyed at Rohtang viewpoint)
lunch.location_note: Mid‑way on Rohtang Pass, approx 2 hrs from Manali base

dinner.description: Mild Himachali dal with plain rice – soothing after altitude exposure
Mutton curry with naan – hearty family option
Fine‑dining experience at a hotel restaurant – cedar‑smoked duck with apple compote

days.notes: Rohtang requires a permit (₹550/vehicle) booked 1–2 days ahead; carry Diamox for altitude sickness. Return before 1 PM to avoid evening traffic.

activities.name: Leisure walk through Old Manali – cafés, riverbank benches, boutique shops
Drive to Atal Tunnel viewpoint – short stop for photos of the 8.8 km tunnel entrance

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – dosa with coconut chutney and sambar

lunch.description: Veg thali (dal, rice, chapati, bhindi) at a roadside eatery near Old Manali
lunch.location_note: ≈2 km from the Old Manali café strip

dinner.description: Himachali siddu (steamed wheat dumplings) with ghee – local treat
Butter chicken with pulao – crowd‑pleaser for friends
Upscale lounge dinner – grilled lamb kebabs with mint yogurt dip

days.notes: Relaxed day after the high‑altitude Rohtang visit; suitable walking distances for a small group.

activities.name: Final stroll on Mall Road – pick up souvenirs, enjoy local tea
Drive back to Delhi – depart early to avoid night‑time mountain driving

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – idli with sambar and coconut chutney

lunch.description: Highway dhaba thali – dal, rice, roti, salad
lunch.location_note: midway near Mandi, approx 250 km from Manali

dinner.description: Light snack on the road – samosa and tea (if needed)
Simple pasta with tomato sauce – easy group option
No premium dinner – travel day focus on safe arrival

days.notes: Wrap up the trip with souvenir shopping; ensure vehicle check before long return drive.

warnings: Rohtang Pass requires a government permit (₹550/vehicle) – book 1‑2 days in advance via rohtangpermits.nic.in; unofficial agents charge up to ₹2,000.
Altitude at Rohtang (≈4,000 m) can cause sickness – carry Diamox, stay hydrated, and limit strenuous exertion.
No Uber/Ola in Manali – negotiate private taxi fares beforehand; shared taxis cost around ₹100‑150 per seat, private hires ₹700‑900 for a round‑trip to Solang.
Roads may be congested after 10 AM at Rohtang and Solang; aim to depart Manali by 7 AM to beat crowds.
Winter‑type snowfall can linger in May at higher passes; pack warm layers and waterproof shoes.

Fake Rohtang permit agents near Manali hotels charge ₹1,500–2,000 claiming the portal is full; the official portal (rohtangpermits.nic.in) is straightforward and cancellations free up slots daily – book the permit yourself 1–2 days ahead.
Rohtang Pass requires a permit costing ₹550/vehicle (non‑Himachal registered) with a daily cap of 1,200 diesel + 800 petrol vehicles – book early to secure entry.
Altitude at Rohtang (3,978 m) has no medical facility within 30 km; solo travellers should carry Diamox (acetazolamide) and be aware of altitude sickness symptoms.
No Ola or Uber – taxi union controls all cabs. Negotiate fare before boarding to avoid overcharging.
Manali → Solang Valley round‑trip private taxi costs ₹700–900; shared taxi costs ₹100–150 per seat (from HRTC bus stand). Ensure you agree on price beforehand.
Rohtang Pass full‑day taxi price ranges ₹2,500–3,500 – compare with private hire rates before committing.
Crowds at Rohtang and Solang build after 10 AM; depart Manali by 7 AM to beat congestion (entry window closes at 1 PM).
Steep stairs at Hadimba Devi Temple and 200 m uneven stone paving may be challenging if you carry heavy luggage; consider using a luggage trolley or limiting gear.

Photo tout risk at Hadimba Temple: men with Himachali caps and yaks position themselves on the approach path. Once a cap is placed on a child, they demand ₹300–500. Decline before physical contact — walk past without eye contact.
personalization_notes: Adventure‑focused activities (paragliding, Rohtang pass, Solang ropeway) match your stated interest in nature and thrill.
Mid‑range budget keeps accommodation and meals comfortable without luxury overspend, fitting the ‘medium’ budget preference.
Group of three friends benefits from shared transport and flexible dining options, allowing both local flavours and premium experiences.
